articles.title: Inside Netflix’s creative clearout.
articles.summary:

articles.title: Assam trains 73 excise officers to crack down on illicit liquor trade
articles.summary: Assam launches 30-day residential training for 73 excise officers at Lachit Borphukan Police Academy to boost raids, investigations and curb illicit liquor trade.
articles.body: Guwahati: Assam has launched a 30-day residential training programme for 73 excise enforcement officers to strengthen the crackdown on illegal liquor networks, improve field operations and protect public health.The programme was inaugurated at the Lachit Borphukan Police Academy in Dergaon on Monday by excise commissioner and secretary Virendra Mittal, who stressed discipline, technical precision and commitment to public service during enforcement operations.The intensive month-long curriculum is structured to improve physical endurance, modern investigation methods, raid management, and legal compliance, with the aim of improving officers’ operational readiness and effectiveness against illegal liquor syndicates and tax evasion.Senior excise officer Sailendra Pandey said the programme would enhance officers’ field capabilities and equip them with improved legal and technological skills to tackle illicit liquor networks.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.title: Jamshedpur police arrest 15 for gambling, seize cash and phones
articles.summary: Jamshedpur police arrest 15 in Prakash Nagar gambling raid; seize 16 smartphones, Rs 7.67 lakh cash, cards; DC orders tougher anti-drug action, hotspot surveillance.
articles.body: Jamshedpur: A total of 15 people were arrested on charges of gambling from a house located in Prakash Nagar under the Birsanagar police station limits on Monday. A total of 16 smartphones, Rs 7,67,400 in cash, and several decks of playing cards were seized during the operation, police said.Attending a Narcotics Coordination Committee (NCORD) meeting earlier in the day, East Singhbhum deputy commissioner (DC) Rajiv Ranjan directed police and departments concerned to step up action against drug trafficking and strengthen surveillance in identified narcotics hotspots.“Strict legal action must be taken against those involved in drug trafficking and illegal drug trade. Sensitive areas should be monitored regularly, and there should be no unnecessary delays in investigations or legal proceedings. All departments concerned must work in coordination to identify and dismantle drug networks operating in the district,” DC Ranjan said.Enforcement and monitoring were under way at 10 hotspots. In September, action under the NDPS Act led to the seizure of 133 kg ganja and 52 packets of brown sugar, officials said.The education department and local police stations were directed to continue anti-drug programmes in schools. “Anti-drug awareness programmes should be conducted regularly in schools and colleges to educate students about the harmful effects of drugs on health, families and society,” DC stated.Urging residents to report narcotics sale on helpline 112 or police control room 0657-2431028, the DC stressed that de-addiction, treatment and rehabilitation services must remain accessible and effective for people affected by substance abuse.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: Rs 799 kurti that never came, but led cops to Rs 30-crore cyber frauds
articles.summary: Delhi Police cracked a Rs 30-crore cyber fraud network after a DU student’s Rs 799 kurti order led to multiple payments; seven arrested, devices seized.
articles.body: New Delhi: A routine online shopping order for a kurti worth Rs 799 led Delhi Police to unearth an alleged cyber fraud syndicate that channelled credit transactions worth over Rs 30 crore through a network of bank accounts. Seven people have been arrested.The probe began after a student of Delhi University’s Ramjas College was allegedly cheated of Rs 6,450 by an online seller who repeatedly demanded payments on the pretext of facilitating a parcel delivery. Following an analysis of nearly 200 mobile numbers and IMEIs, police traced the money trail to Greater Noida and Kanpur. Police have linked 27 cyber fraud complaints from different states to the network.The student had come across an advertisement for a kurti on a social media platform. She was redirected to WhatsApp, where she placed an order worth Rs 799 and paid Rs 400 in advance through a QR code. She later received a call for a passcode for delivery. On contacting the seller, she was allegedly induced to pay Rs 1,150 as a refundable charge for generating the code, followed by payments of Rs 2,000, Rs 2,650 and Rs 650 on similar pretexts. The parcel never arrived and no money was refunded, police said.DCP (north) Niharika Bhatt said investigators analysed banking transactions and digital records obtained from companies. The cheated amount was traced through a merchant account to a bank account linked to a firm in Greater Noida.Sustained surveillance led to coordinated raids in Greater Noida on Oct 16, resulting in the arrest of Aditya Mishra (23), Ayush Verma (22), Abhishek Pal (23), Himanshu Rana (29), Rahul Kumar (30) and Gaurav Pandey (24). Udit Pratap Singh Bhadauriya (22) was arrested in Kanpur on Oct 21.Police said searches at rented premises in Greater Noida led them to three suspected firms. Investigators claimed that the firms were used to open bank accounts that were subsequently supplied to cyber fraudsters.Mishra allegedly said he, Bhadauriya, Verma and Pal had set up the firms and opened current accounts, which were handed over to Rana and Kumar for a monthly payment of Rs 25,000. The two allegedly supplied the accounts, along with banking kits and linked SIM cards, to Pandey, an MBA graduate.Pandey allegedly operated a bank account supply network and provided the accounts to individuals identified as Maxwell and Solitaire on a commission basis. Police said the two communicated through WhatsApp numbers bearing the US country code. The accounts were allegedly used to receive and route money obtained through cyber fraud.Mishra and Bhadauriya are BBA graduates, while Verma holds a BCA degree, Pal has an ITI qualification, and Rana and Kumar are BA graduates.Police seized 20 mobile phones, 45 SIM cards, 39 point-of-sale machines, 33 debit cards, 28 cheque books, 15 scanners and two laptops, besides banking documents.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Anthropic IPO live updates: S-1 filing discloses $16.3B in first-half revenue, plans to list as 'ANT'
articles.summary: Anthropic has publicly filed its S-1 investor prospectus.
articles.body: Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) publicly filed its S-1 investor prospectus on Monday, ahead of its planned initial public offering later this fall under the ticker symbol “ANT.”The AI lab, helmed by CEO Dario Amodei, has exploded in popularity thanks to its Claude Code AI coding tool and Claude Cowork enterprise offering.As of May, Anthropic was valued at $965 billion, more than rival OpenAI's (OPAI.PVT) $852 billion valuation in March.Anthropic's S-1 provides potential investors with their first look at the company's financials, including how much it's spending on capital expenditures related to AI chips and data center leases, as well as how much revenue it's bringing in and what its largest sources are.The AI lab has faced a number of controversies this year, including a run-in with the Trump administration over how the government can use the company's AI models, and current and former employees warning about the potential threat of killer AI. Though experts say those fears are overblown.

articles.title: Instagram chases YouTube with a push for longer, widescreen videos
articles.summary: Instagram is announcing a big push into longform horizontal video, which the platform is calling “Features.” It’s also testing several other video features and has been expanding its TV app.
articles.body: Instagram is announcing a big push into longform horizontal video, which the platform is calling “Features.” Instagram boss Adam Mosseri has been against doing longform video on the platform “for a long time,” he says in a six-and-a-half-minute video (here’s the widescreen version) with VP of product Tessa Lyons, saying that “one of my concerns has been, how do we make sure that we keep Instagram not just about entertainment, but about connecting with friends. If you watch a longform video, that’s “it’s a lot of Reels, photos, and carousels that you might not have sent to a friend,” meaning less likes and shares. [Media: Now, though, the team is working on making shortform and longform video “symbiotic,” according to Mosseri, like podcasts or comedy specials that can be both long videos and broken up into shorter ones. The announcement of this widescreen video push also follows the launch of Instagram’s TV app late last year. That app launched first as a Reels-focused experience and as a pilot for Amazon Fire TV devices in the US, but it’s since expanded to Google TVs, Samsung TVs and Apple TV, and Instagram launched new features like the ability to watch Stories earlier this year. Mosseri also talked about the updates with creators Samir Chaudry and Colin Rosenblum, and their video includes some clips of how longform video will show up on the platform. [Media: Today, Features are expanding to the US in a small test and is in testing with some creators in Brazil, according to Instagram spokesperson Megan Buckley. Instagram is testing a few other video-focused features as well, including clips pointing to a long video, a way for creators to create a “series” of Reels, and improvements for live video discovery.

articles.title: Cowboys vs. Eagles score, live updates: Saquon Barkley returns as Eagles, without Jalen Hurts, try to snap 4-game skid in NFC East showdown
articles.summary: The Cowboys and Eagles both enter the week at 2-4 in a wide-open NFC East.
articles.body: The Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles will close out the Week 7 game slate on "Monday Night Football" in an NFC East showdown at Lincoln Financial Field, with kickoff set for 8:15 p.m. ET.Both franchises enter the week at 2-4 after disappointing starts to the year, but the division remains wide open as the New York Giants lead with a 3-2-1 record.The Cowboys are coming off a disappointing Sunday night loss to the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. After struggling on defense for most of the season, Dallas couldn't get their offense going, stuck at just seven points before scoring a touchdown in garbage time with just 0:44 on the clock.The Eagles, meanwhile, had their season turned upside down last week after quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve as he undergoes treatment for deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in his lungs. Now, it's up to quarterback Tanner McKee to save the season. He threw for 215 yards and one touchdown in his third career start last week.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles close out Week 7 on "Monday Night Football," airing on ABC and ESPN.

articles.title: WNBA Finals live updates, Dream-Valkyries box score: Gabby Williams, Golden State look for series lead over Angel Reese, Atlanta
articles.summary: The WNBA Finals head back to Ballhalla for Game 5 on Monday night.
articles.body: The Golden State Valkyries halted what appeared to be significant momentum for the Atlanta Dream toward their first championship by winning Game 4 to even up the WNBA Finals.Tied at 2-2, the Finals now becomes a best-of-three series with two of those games on the Valkyries' home court at Chase Center in San Francisco, beginning with Monday's pivotal Game 5. A key factor for Golden State in Game 4 was controlling Angel Reese. After recording double-doubles in each of the series' first three games, the Dream forward was held to 8 points and 9 rebounds with 6 turnovers. How she responds to that, and tough defense by the Valkyries' Kiah Stokes, could determine Atlanta's success for the next two to three games. On the other side, Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase changed the starting lineup for Game 4, swapping Tiffany Hayes and Kaila Charles for Kayla Thornton and Cecilia Zandalasini. Considering the tighter defense and increased pace created, Golden State will probably stick with that for Game 5. Meanwhile, Atlanta will try to find an answer for defending Gabby Williams (averaging 18 points per game). Game 5 of the 2026 WNBA Finals between the Dream and Valkyries will begin Monday at 8 p.m. ET on USA Network and CNBC, also streaming on Peacock. articles.title: Brewers vs. Rays live updates, World Series score: ALCS MVP Freddy Peralta, Robert Gasser to start Game 3
articles.summary: The Brewers hold a 2-0 lead over the Rays as the World Series moves to Tropicana Field for Game 3.
articles.body: The Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays are back for Game 3 of the World Series, with first pitch at 8 p.m. ET Monday at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida.The Rays find themselves in an 0-2 hole as they head home after a disastrous unraveling in Game 2. In that one, Tampa Bay jumped to a four-run lead in the top of the first but didn't score again, and the Brewers chipped away. Sal Frelick tied the game with a leadoff homer in the sixth, and Cooper Pratt drove in Brice Turang with the go-ahead run in the seventh for a 5-4 win.In Game 3, the Brewers will lean on left-hander Robert Gasser (5-5, 3.87 ERA). He most recently threw five scoreless innings against the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 3 of the NLCS, allowing 3 hits and 1 walk while striking out 3 in a 6-2 victory.The Rays will counter with right-hander Freddy Peralta (10-11, 4.42 ERA), who was named ALCS MVP after allowing just 1 earned run on 9 hits with 9 strikeouts over 12 innings in three appearances, including two starts, against the Cleveland Guardians.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Rays host the Brewers in Game 3 of the World Series, airing on Fox.

articles.title: Hasan Piker sues Scott Jennings for defamation
articles.summary: Progressive Twitch streamer Hasan Piker filed a defamation lawsuit against conservative CNN commentator Scott Jennings on Tuesday, accusing him of falsely cl...
articles.body:
Progressive Twitch streamer Hasan Piker filed a defamation lawsuit against conservative CNN commentator Scott Jennings on Tuesday, accusing him of falsely claiming Piker advocated for lynching Black Americans after airing an edited video of his remarks.

The 38-page lawsuit, filed in federal court in Washington, D.C., centers on an Aug. 11 episode of "The Scott Jennings Show," in which Jennings shared clips of Piker claiming he had said, "the USA should resume lynchings against Black people."

Piker, who threatened legal action in August over the claim and shared further context to the clips, alleges Jennings knowingly misrepresented sarcastic comments he made during his livestreams by turning it into an apparent endorsement of racial violence.

"Mr. Jennings did not merely mischaracterize something Mr. Piker said," the complaint reads. "He took a false, fabricated, and manipulated video of Mr. Piker, added a made-up quotation that Mr. Piker never uttered, and then made accusations that went beyond even what the manipulated footage purported to show."

During the August broadcast, Jennings warned Black voters to pay close attention before playing the clip, which included an on-screen caption attributing a statement, "Let's go back to a better time when lynchings were happening," to Piker.

Jennings later accused Piker of "calling for Black voters to be lynched" and referred to what he called "the Piker plan of returning our country to lynchings."

The original footage came from an October 2024 Twitch broadcast in which Piker was reacting to a debate between two Black political commentators — one liberal and one conservative. After the conservative participant criticized "woke DAs," Piker sarcastically suggested the commentator wanted to return to an era of racial discrimination and lynchings, according to the complaint.

"He said, 'We need more Klansmen, OK? Can we go back to a better time when lynchings were happening?'" Piker said during the stream in reaction to the commentator's argument.

Piker's attorneys argue that the edited video removed the words "He said," along with his laughter and surrounding commentary, to intentionally make it appear as though Piker was expressing his own beliefs rather than mocking someone else's.

The dispute emerged amid the Michigan Senate race , where the edited video was circulated to criticize progressive Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed over his association with Piker.

When Jennings posted the segment on the social platform X, he referred to Piker as El-Sayed's "best pal and campaign partner," before accusing him of supporting racial violence.

The post has received roughly 2.5 million views as of Tuesday, according to the lawsuit, and Jennings allegedly refused to retract his statements despite receiving a written demand from Piker's attorneys on Aug. 31.

Piker's legal team also says the accusations damaged his reputation and threatened his ability to earn money through streaming, advertising and sponsorships.

articles.title: Brewers vs. Rays live updates, World Series lineups, where to watch: Brewers one win from first championship in franchise history
articles.summary: The Brewers can sweep the Rays in the World Series with a win Tuesday.
articles.body: The Tampa Bay Rays have dug themselves into a deep, deep hole heading into Game 4 of the 2026 World Series, as the Milwaukee Brewers hold a 3-0 series lead and are one win from the first championship in franchise history. A win would also make Milwaukee the first team to sweep the World Series since the 2012 San Francisco Giants and the first to sweep both the League Championship Series and the World Series since the LCS became a best-of-seven in 1985.First pitch is set for 8 p.m. ET Tuesday at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida.The Brewers continued their dismantling of the Rays with a 10-1 win in Game 3 on Monday. Starting pitcher Robert Gasser allowed just one hit over six scoreless innings, facing the minimum, and Milwaukee broke it open with an eight-run fifth inning to take a 10-0 lead. By the time Tampa Bay got on the board in the ninth, the damage had long been done.In Game 4, the Brewers will hand the ball to right-hander Dustin May (7-9, 4.70 ERA) with a chance to clinch. May's last start came in Milwaukee's lone loss this postseason, Game 3 of the NLDS against the San Diego Padres, in which he allowed 3 hits and 2 earned runs while striking out 3 over 3 innings.The Rays will counter with right-hander Griffin Jax (8-10, 3.53 ERA) with their season on the line. He'll hope to improve on his previous start against the Cleveland Guardians in the ALCS, in which he allowed 5 hits and 3 earned runs over 4 innings, including the go-ahead, two-run homer by Petey Halpin. Jax has a 6.00 ERA in six innings this postseason, including two in relief against the New York Yankees in the ALDS.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Rays host the Brewers in Game 4 of the World Series.

articles.title: Cucurella confiesa el futbolista del Atlético con el que se pegaría: "Saca lo peor de mí... Le reviento"
articles.standfirst: Marc Cucurella le asegura a Ibai Llanos que "reviento" a Álex Baena en un combate de boxeo y el futbolista del Atlético acepta el reto
articles.summary: Marc Cucurella le asegura a Ibai Llanos que "reviento" a Álex Baena en un combate de boxeo y el futbolista del Atlético acepta el reto
articles.body: Marc Cucurella, lateral del Real Madrid, le confesó a Ibai Llanos con quién se pegaría en la famosa 'La Velada del Año' que organiza el popular 'streamer'. "¿Si te tuvieras que pegar en una velada de boxeo, contra quién te pegarías?", le preguntó el famoso 'streamer' a Kylian Mbappé, Unai Simón, Ronaldo Nazario, David Raya, Luis Díaz, Luis Figo, Unai Simón y Marc Cucurella la alfombra roja de la Gala del Balón de Oro. Mpappé contestó que "conozco desde hace pocos meses tu evento y ahora sí lo conozco. ¿Contra quién participaría? Contra ti, pero te dejo ganar". Luis Figo contestó que se enfrentaría "con Ronaldo Nazario", y por su parte Ronaldo replicó que "estaría bien enfrentarse con Figo, no sabe nada de boxeo". "Llevo mucho tiempo entrenando boxeo. Me enfrentaría con cualquiera, tengo buenas manos", subrayó el mítico futbolista brasileño. Luis Díaz pelearía "con Daniel Muñoz, le daría unos cortitos", David Raya "con Rodri", Unai Simón "contra ti (Ibai Llanos), con el mordisco en la oreja". Marc Cucurella le contestó a Ibai Llanos que "cambiaría, la cobra la dejo en paz" y que en la velada de boxeo se enfrentaría a "Álex Baena". "Álex Baena es amigo mío, pero saca lo peor de mí", apuntó el defensa campeón del Mundial con España junto a Baena. "Le reviento", subrayó Cucurella. Álex Baena aceptó el reto pugilístico de Cucurella y contestó al futbolista del Real Madrid en Instagram: "Cuando quieras , sitio día y hora".

articles.title: Control de mago, vaselina y por la escuadra: Ibai 'rescata' al Marcelo más espectacular a sus 38 años
articles.standfirst: El creador de contenido 'fichaba' al brasileño para su último vídeo
articles.summary: El creador de contenido 'fichaba' al brasileño para su último vídeo
articles.body: Ibai Llanos lleva mucho tiempo consiguiendo lo imposible en el sector de la creación de contenido, pero en su último vídeo nos ha regalado un contenido increíble para los amantes del fútbol. El contexto es muy sencillo, un seguidor le pedía ayuda para ganar un partido en una de las peores ligas de Cataluña en cuanto a nivel, ya que ya el año pasado quedaban últimos y en los dos primeros partidos de la temporada también se les resistía la victoria. Pues bien, a Ibai Llanos no se le ocurría otra cosa que fichar a Marcelo para hacer que este equipo llamado Los Resbalados FC intentara llevarse los primeros tres puntos. La leyenda del Real Madrid ayudaba a los chicos con un mensaje de unión y equipo, pero su función, que era ganar el partido, la cumplió a la perfección aunque también tuvo tiempo para 'espabilar' a los chavales y echar alguna que otra bronca. Y sí, es cierto que, como decía el propio Marcelo, con 38 años las piernas no van como antes y el despliegue físico que vimos del brasileño no fue el más exigente, pero cuando la pelota llevaba a sus pies sentimos lo que tantas veces hemos sentido viendo jugar a la leyenda del fútbol. Con el marcador 0-2 un compañero recuperaba en la frontal y Marcelo, haciendo ver como si no costara nada, endosaba de primeras un latigazo a la derecha del portero imparable. Pero la verdadera magia llegaba después. Para empatar el encuentro Marcelo se inventaba una de sus jugadas. Conducía por el centro del campo y solo una bicicleta le bastaba para acomodarse el balón a su pierna izquierda y hacer un tiro directo a la escuadra derecha. Y para culminar la remontada el brasileño nos dejaba una acción al alcance de muy pocos. El portero sacaba en largo y tras un control perfecto se quedaba solo ante el guardameta rival, y como solo los genios hacen en un espacio tan corto, picaba el balón y remontaba un partido que parecía imposible, por lo menos, para los mortales como nosotros.

articles.title: Instagram doesn’t have a plan to pay long-form video creators
articles.summary: Instagram is testing long-form videos to lure in creatives from YouTube, but the platform hasn’t figured out how (or if) it’ll actually pay them.
articles.body: Instagram is testing long-form videos (again) to lure in creatives from YouTube, but the platform hasn’t figured out how (or if) it’ll actually pay them. After Instagram head Adam Mosseri announced Features on Monday, creators immediately started voicing their complaints on Threads and Reddit about the lack of monetization opportunities, compared to the ad share and performance-based incentives provided by YouTube. Mosseri addressed the monetization concerns in a Threads post yesterday, saying “We understand the economics matter a ton, and are exploring multiple options to help long-form creators get paid.” It’s anyone’s guess what those solutions will look like. In one post on Threads, creator Sidneyraz (real name Sidney Raskind) said it feels like Mosseri and Meta are “just making fun of us” by not giving creators the ability to place long-form monetization ads into Features videos. “Y’all know how this works and you know how ad calls work and you know that long form creators need ad rev to survive but you’re ask[ing] them all to upload long form content for free just to live on your platform,” Raskind said. “That’s insane.” [Media: The new Features format is currently being tested by a small group of creators in the US and Brazil. Features videos can be up to 90 minutes long (compared to the 20-minute max for Reels), and seemingly focus on landscape content instead of vertical, making them a good fit for Instagram’s TV apps as it tries to snare our attention across more screens. Meta does have some limited monetization tools for Reels, but these don’t pay creators directly per view like YouTube does. “What’s funny about Instagram adding long-form video and reels that link to the long form is the complete lack of any sort of monetization,” tech creator M. Brandon Lee said on Threads. “Why should I post my long form there? What benefit does it bring me? I can’t even post links in my content to make affiliate income unless I PAY you to post a LIMITED number of links. I can’t get ad share revenue. You want more but don’t give more.” While some longer-form video creators on Facebook previously reported good earnings via its old ad revenue-sharing payout model, Meta retired this in 2024 when it switched to a performance-based system. The primary incentive to post a Features video is the reach of Instagram, but the tradeoff is knowing that Meta will use it to train its AI models. Google considers YouTube videos free game for AI training too, of course, but at least creators get paid by the platform. [Media: Speaking on a podcast with Samir Chaudry and Colin Rosenblum, Mosseri said introducing pre-roll or mid-roll ads is “going to be problematic from a user experience perspective,” and that it doesn’t make sense to scale up the small existing performance-based program because Meta spends more money on it than it makes back. “There are three ways you can get paid at a high level: you can get paid by the platform directly, you can get paid by a fan, and you can get paid by a brand. Right now how it works on Instagram primarily is that you get paid by brands, some people get paid by fans,” Mosseri said. “Creators don’t produce a lot more when we pay, compared to what they already create.”

articles.body: Progressive Twitch streamer Hasan Piker filed a defamation lawsuit against conservative CNN commentator Scott Jennings on Tuesday, accusing him of falsely claiming Piker advocated for lynching Black Americans after airing an edited video of his remarks. The 38-page lawsuit, filed in federal court in Washington, D.C., centers on an Aug. 11 episode of “The Scott Jennings Show,” in which Jennings shared clips of Piker claiming he had said, “the USA should resume lynchings against Black people.”

articles.title: Six women from Bangladesh rescued from brothels in Budhwar Peth in Pune; had been promised jobs but were forced into prostitution
articles.summary: Pune police rescued six Bangladeshi women from Budhwar Peth brothels; lured with job promises, trafficked without documents, forced into prostitution.
articles.body: Pune: Six women from Bangladesh were rescued from different brothels located in the red-light area of Budhwar Peth in the early hours of Wednesday.Faraskhana police registered a case later in the day against four persons for pushing the women into prostitution. They have detained two agents accused in the case, while the other two who have been identified are on the run.Deputy commissioner of police (Zone I) Krushikesh Rawale formed a joint team of Faraskhana, Vishrambaug and Khadak police stations and raided these brothels after receiving a tip-off. An officer said, “These women were brought to Pune from Bangladesh about four months ago. They did not have valid documents or ID cards. They told us the agents helped them to cross the border and promised lucrative jobs in Mumbai and other cities. However, they brought these women to Pune and sold them to the brothel keepers.”Earlier this year, in March, Pune city police had rescued four Bangladeshi women from a brothel in Budhwar Peth. articles.title: WNBA Finals: Dream rediscover 3-point stroke, force Game 7 after riding dominant first half to resurgent win over Valkyries
articles.summary: Behind Allisha Gray's five triples, Atlanta made 13 shots from beyond the arc on Thursday.
articles.body: Atlanta Dream guard Allisha Gray came out firing on Thursday in Game 6 of the WNBA Finals and finished with 23 points and five 3s in an 80-69 win over the Golden State Valkyries on Oct. 29 at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, Georgia. (AP Photo/Brynn Anderson)AP Photo/Brynn AndersonThe Atlanta Dream knocked down just six 3-pointers during their Game 5 defeat to the Golden State Valkyries in this year’s WNBA Finals. Karl Smesko’s team netted that many triples in the first quarter of Game 6 three days later on Thursday afternoon in front of a home crowd that was raucous as ever despite the much-discussed early tip-off.Atlanta’s first field goal was an Allisha Gray 3-pointer. That was a harbinger. The Dream went 6 of 8 from beyond the arc in the opening frame and wrapped the day with 13 makes from outside.Their 3-point barrage fueled an offensive resurgence. After scoring only 62 and 55 points in Games 4 and 5, both losses, the Dream piled up 32 in the first quarter alone, en route to a 17-point advantage. A 22-point second half from Gabby Williams inspired a late-game push from the Valkyries, but Gray’s fifth and final 3-pointer restored the Dream’s double-digit lead, and Atlanta forced the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history with a series-tying 80-69 win.The winner-take-all game will be played Saturday at 8 p.m. ET in Golden State’s Chase Center. Both the Dream and Valkyries are one win away from their first WNBA title in franchise history.Gray, who has been battling through a left hand injury, finished with a team-high 23 points on Thursday. She shot 5 of 7 from 3-point land. Rhyne Howard was 4 of 6 from long range and wasn’t far behind Gray on the stat sheet, registering 21 points. Although Angel Reese shot just 5 of 18 from the floor, she scored 15 points — the total she combined for the previous two games — and, with 14 rebounds, she notched her fourth double-double of the series. That’s the second most double-doubles any player has recorded in a single WNBA Finals.Missed layups haunted Golden State in the early going. Williams wasn’t exempt from those struggles. Still, she persevered to mount a game-high 26 points and draw the Valkyries within eight points with 1:15 to go.Game 6 tipped off just after its expected start time of 12:30 p.m. ET. When and where exactly in Atlanta the matchup was going to be held was previously up in the air due to fan demand and scheduling complications, namely the fact that State Farm Arena — which seats approximately 13,500 more people than the Dream’s home venue but has hosted the team’s games throughout its postseason run — was already going to be the site of an Atlanta Hawks regular-season game Thursday night.So in order for the stadium to fit both games in on Thursday, Dream-Valkyries had to be played early, a controversial compromise. Dream ownership clarified this week that, months ago, as well as again during the playoffs, it raised concerns about schedule conflicts like this one. Those concerns, according to Dream ownership, “did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved.”There was no rushed championship celebration Thursday afternoon, however. The Dream stretched the series, keeping their title hopes alive.This story is being updated.

articles.title: The director of Obsession put a new horror short on YouTube
articles.summary: Curry Barker, the director behind the hit horror film Obsession, just published a new horror short on YouTube titled “Mama Bear.”
articles.body: Curry Barker, the director behind the hit horror film Obsession, just published a new horror short on YouTube. The short, titled “Mama Bear,” is nearly five minutes long. The video is pretty unnerving, and fair warning that it gets a little graphic, but it’s a fun one to watch if you’re looking for something scary ahead of Halloween on Saturday. Barker wrote, directed, and edited “Mama Bear,” according to the description for the video, which was published on his that’s a bad idea YouTube channel. The description also has a note thanking Windows for “sponsoring this short film,” and Barker was featured in an Instagram video earlier this week with a Surface laptop. Barker will follow Obsession with Anything but Ghosts, which debuts in May 2027. Horror is big business right now, with the film Backrooms, directed by YouTuber Kane Parsons, also proving to be a big box office success this year. Parsons debuted a new Backrooms YouTube episode in August.

articles.title: Panthers vs. Packers live updates, inactives, where to watch: Jordan Love, Green Bay look to rebound on 'Thursday Night Football' vs. Bryce Young, Carolina
articles.summary: The Panthers and Packers will both look to bounce back from Week 7 losses in primetime this week.
articles.body: The Carolina Panthers and Green Bay Packers will open up Week 8 on "Thursday Night Football," with kickoff set for 8:15 p.m. ET at Lambeau Field. The game will air on Prime Video.Despite just a 3-3 record, the Panthers hold the lead in the NFC South thanks to a tie-breaker over the Atlanta Falcons. They'll look to bounce back after an embarrassing home blowout against their division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers last week, where they lost 43-13 with a season-high four turnovers. The Bucs won that game with just 64 total passing yards as Carolina struggled to stop the run, giving up 258 yards on the ground. Adding insult to injury (literally), starting right tackle Taylor Moton suffered a fractured fibula in Week 7 in just his second game back from a blood clot. The Packers will also look to bounce back after a Week 7 loss to the Detroit Lions 20-17 thanks to a walk-off field goal from Detroit kicker Jake Bates. Green Bay will have plenty of opportunity on offense this week after seeing how the Bucs exploited the run game against the Panthers, with Josh Jacobs in his second game back after being activated from the commissioner's exempt list. Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Panthers and Packers open up Week 8 on "Thursday Night Football," airing on Amazon Prime Video.
